brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix unveil $950B U.S. supply deals; DRAM/NAND rally extends Q3 with 20–30% / 35–40% QoQ hikes; CoWoS sold out through 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="22-2,22-3,22-4">Samsung and SK Hynix announced combined $950 billion memory-chip supply partnerships with U.S. tech firms, with SK Hynix providing $750 billion to Nvidia and others while Samsung will supply $200 billion to Broadcom.</cite> <cite index="15-1,15-2">DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 10–15% QoQ, with ADATA citing 20–30% DRAM and 35–40% NAND increases.</cite> <cite index="35-1,35-3">Hyperscalers are guiding to roughly $725 billion in combined 2026 capex, up 77% from ~$410 billion in 2025.</cite> <cite index="38-2,38-5">TSMC CEO confirmed CoWoS capacity remains "extremely tight and sold out through 2026," with the supply-demand gap expected to narrow from 20% to roughly 10% by year-end.</cite> <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix is projected to maintain a ~50% HBM market share in 2026.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%.</cite> <cite index="5-4">Nvidia is negotiating with all three HBM suppliers, including SK Hynix and Samsung, with possible pricing pushback as Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification.</cite> Long SK Hynix vs. short Samsung: Hynix maintains HBM qualification lead with Nvidia Rubin and secured the bulk of the $750B in long-term agreements. Samsung's 22% HBM share trails badly despite $200B Broadcom deal focused on custom processors. <cite index="6-1,6-4">Samsung and SK Hynix stock prices have soared 114% and 186% year-to-date respectively.</cite> Relative outperformance by Hynix justified by structural HBM positioning; pair unwinds if Samsung accelerates HBM3E/HBM4 certifications or if memory pricing peaks earlier than consensus 2027.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-1,16-10">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93–98% QoQ in Q1 2026, with buyers paying roughly double what they paid three months earlier.</cite> <cite index="11-1,15-2">Q3 2026 contract prices projected at +13–18% DRAM, +10–15% NAND QoQ, decelerating from Q1/Q2 record increases.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected to last through 2027, giving leading suppliers stronger pricing power than historically typical.</cite> <cite index="8-1,8-10">Manufacturers are diverting production lines toward HBM stacks and enterprise-grade DDR5, squeezing supply of flash and mobile memory.</cite> Enterprise demand robust; consumer pricing resistance building. Deceleration in QoQ increases signals cycle maturation but no turn yet.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="8-4,8-12">Top three memory makers have already allocated their full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding for a 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments are projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits.</cite> <cite index="42-2">Based on Q3 earnings calls from SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung, HBM supply is fully allocated through 2026, including HBM3E.</cite> <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only a minimal to modest downtick in HBM3E pricing for 2026 compared with 2025.</cite> <cite index="42-7">Samsung expects high-teens to low-20% price increases for HBM in 2026 contracts.</cite> Nvidia Rubin/Vera architecture driving HBM4 pull-in; SK Hynix mass-producing HBM4 while Samsung remains in qualification. Structural supply shortage intact through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix unveil $950B U.S. chip supply partnerships during Korean president's Silicon Valley visit
news_pulse.implication: Locks in multi-year revenue visibility for both; SK Hynix $750B to Nvidia/hyperscalers, Samsung $200B to Broadcom. Underscores U.S. dependence on Korean memory (80–90% of demand). Validates HBM capex cycle extending through 2028+.

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns DRAM prices up 20–30%, NAND up 35–40% in Q3 2026 as AI starves consumer supply
news_pulse.implication: Confirms memory pricing rally extends into Q3 despite deceleration from Q1's 93–98% QoQ spike. Consumer affordability limits emerging; enterprise/server demand remains insulated. Module makers benefit from inventory revaluation.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers guiding $725B combined 2026 capex, up 77% YoY; Amazon ~$200B, Google $175–185B, Meta $115–135B, Microsoft ~$120B
news_pulse.implication: ~75% allocated to AI infrastructure (~$450B AI-specific). Validates memory/HBM demand through 2027; supply-constrained not demand-constrained. Pricing power intact for Samsung/Hynix/Micron. Risk: ROI scrutiny if enterprise AI adoption stalls.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CEO confirms CoWoS "extremely tight and sold out through 2026"; capacity target 120–140K wpm by year-end, up from 35K in late 2024
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing but still 10% undersupplied by end-2026. Nvidia locked ~60% of capacity; AMD/others fighting for remainder. Directly gates HBM-attached GPU/accelerator shipments. 2027 target: 200K wpm.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix controlled 57% global HBM revenue share Q4 2025; Samsung 22%, Micron 21%
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix HBM dominance intact; Samsung trailing despite capacity adds. Nvidia qualification remains key gatekeeper. Pricing power skewed to Hynix; Samsung must close qual gap to capture Rubin/Vera ramp.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix shares tumbled 7–9% July 2 as chip rout spreads from Wall Street; SK Hynix announces ₩100T ($64B) domestic investment, M17 fab targeted H1 2029
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after YTD rallies (Samsung +114%, Hynix +186%). Memory names now ~50% of KOSPI weight vs. ~25% end-2025, amplifying index volatility. Fundamentals unchanged; capex commitments signal confidence in multi-year upcycle.

news_pulse.headline: Memory price surge cooling as consumers hit affordability limit; Q3 DRAM +13–18%, NAND +10–15% QoQ projected vs. Q1's 93–98% spike
news_pulse.implication: Deceleration ≠ peak; server/HBM demand keeps pricing elevated. Consumer PC/smartphone demand softening; OEMs resisting further increases. Bifurcated market: enterprise pricing power intact, consumer pushback rising. No cyclical turn yet.

news_pulse.headline: Micron HBM4 chips reach >2.8 TB/s bandwidth, designed for Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs; Micron briefly topped $1T market cap in June
news_pulse.implication: HBM4 entering production; Nvidia Rubin (2027+) will drive next capacity/pricing leg. Memory makers capturing record margins (68%+ gross). HBM remains structural bottleneck alongside CoWoS. Validates trillion-dollar valuations for memory pure-plays.

brief.derivatives_signal: Volatility elevated post-July 2 selloff; 30-day historical vol spiking as memory names now dominate KOSPI (50% weight). Options skew likely tilted put-heavy after +114%/+186% YTD runs. No clear directional edge in next 3 hours absent new macro catalyst or earnings pre-announcement. ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) tracking Asia session but illiquid. Watch for reversion-to-mean flows if tech stabilizes in U.S. session.
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI open/close levels—memory names drive 50% of index; any Samsung/Hynix-specific headline will move market
TSMC Q2 earnings (July 16 upcoming)—any update on CoWoS 2H allocation or 2027 capacity guidance reprices AI supply chain
Nvidia/hyperscaler commentary on memory pricing pushback or contract renegotiation—could signal peak pricing
Samsung HBM3E/HBM4 qualification update with Nvidia—closes gap vs. SK Hynix, shifts pair trade dynamics
